message.content:
The Battle of Waterloo (18 June 1815) was one of the bloodiest single-day engagements of the Napoleonic Wars.  Estimates of total casualties (killed, wounded, missing) vary slightly depending on the source, but the most widely cited figures are:

| Side | Casualties (killed, wounded, missing) |
|------|----------------------------------------|
| French & allied (Bourbon & Prussian) | **≈ 25 000** |
| Anglo‑Dutch & Prussian coalition | **≈ 22 000** |
| **Combined total** | **≈ 47 000** |

So, roughly **47,000 soldiers** were lost or rendered unfit for service in the single day of fighting at Waterloo.  These numbers include both immediate battlefield losses and those who later died of wounds or disease.
